specimens.defect: forged struct overlay on a byte buffer, clz(0), and a rotate by the full word width, each in an unguarded function. Compile only; never linked or called. Packing a struct removes padding but does not establish effective type, lifetime, wire version or length, or alignment legality for an overlay forged onto bytes (SEI CERT EXP36-C, EXP39-C); __builtin_clz(0) and a shift by the operand width are undefined (CERT INT34-C). The guarded versions are in bits.c and intrinsics.c

plugin descriptor whose declared size exceeds the octets it provides (FB_PLUGIN_VERSION 4). Independent producer of the plugin descriptor, built as a shared object by a separate compiler invocation so the consumer sees only the wire format and the fb_plugin_copy entry point. FB_PLUGIN_VERSION selects the teaching variant; each descriptor is big-endian: octets 0..1 version, 2..3 total size, 4..7 feature bits, and for version 2 octets 8..11 maximum items
signed overflow checked after the addition has executed. Compile-only: no entry point, no executable golden output

undefined behaviour (out-of-bounds read, uninitialized read, partially initialized read, unsequenced modification, unspecified argument evaluation order). NEVER LINK OR EXECUTE. These functions are translated with -c only. Compiler warnings are observations, not a semantic oracle

constraint violation (table of int pointers passed where an array of three-int rows is required). Compile-only negative translation: the build must be rejected with an "incompatible" diagnostic, never linked
constraint violation (const int * passed where a pointer to a three-int row is required). Compile-only negative translation: the build must be rejected with an "incompatible" diagnostic, never linked

signed overflow, division by zero, unrepresentable quotient (INT_MIN / -1) and normalization overflow, each in an unguarded function. Compile only. No portable golden result and no execution requirement: the functions are never linked into a program or called, because calling them with the dossier's arguments is undefined behaviour (SEI CERT INT32-C, INT33-C). Their guarded counterparts are in integer.c

returns pointers to expired block-scope objects, and reads an indeterminate value. Analysis only: the campaign compiles this file to an object (-c) and never links or calls it. Do not "fix" the defects; the lab teaches how to classify them (see ANALYSIS.md) and how to repair the pattern with caller-owned storage (fv_initialize in views.c)
out-of-bounds reads on purpose for models 0 and 1. HH_MODEL 0: unchecked index; 1: index 4 reachable; 2: checked repair. Analyzed, never run. Do not repair this file; the lab teaches the defect
call with too few arguments to a prototyped function. Translation must be rejected; repair.c is the corrected control. Do not repair this file; the lab teaches the defect
inline function with no external definition (HH_EXTERN=0). Linking fails or succeeds by dialect and optimization; the campaign records which. Do not repair this file; the lab teaches the defect
GNU statement expression (not ISO C). Accepted under -std=gnu17, rejected under strict -std=c17 -Wpedantic. Do not repair this file; the lab teaches the defect
header uses size_t without including <stddef.h>. Works only after a transitive declaration of size_t; see missing_masked.c. Do not repair this file; the lab teaches the defect
conflicting redeclaration (same name, different return type). Translation must be rejected as a constraint violation. Do not repair this file; the lab teaches the defect
unchecked array index (out-of-bounds read for index >= 4). Valid for index 3; index 4 is executed only under AddressSanitizer. Do not repair this file; the lab teaches the defect
unchecked command-line index passed to an unchecked reader. Driver for runtime.c: index 4 is run only in a separate sanitized process. Do not repair this file; the lab teaches the defect
syntax error (unbalanced declarator). Translation must be rejected; the campaign checks the diagnostic. Do not repair this file; the lab teaches the defect
integer converted to pointer without a cast. A constraint violation: strict C17 rejects it, permissive modes only warn. Do not repair this file; the lab teaches the defect

hidden-state probes: parse_char returns a pointer into one static buffer reused by every call, and the other probes expose a signal flag, errno, stdio position, locale and rand state. The lab asks the learner to observe these effects before explaining them; do not repair
counter updated before the trusted authorization check, so a denied request still changes state (flawed path ends at 16, repaired path at 10). Do not repair this file; the drill reviews the defect
returns pointers to objects whose lifetime has ended (block-scope array, compound literal); the closing comment shows an alignment-violating cast. Source analysis only: never linked or run
malloc'd int read without initialization when argv[1][0] != '1'. Tool-experiment target; its output is never a language oracle
local variable read uninitialized on one path. Compile only; never called
four selected faults: escaped automatic object, double free, access after free and overlapping memcpy. Run only under the diagnostic harness, one selector per process
int[2][3] passed where int ** is required (constraint violation). Compile-only negative
integer variable with value zero assigned to a pointer (constraint violation; not a null pointer constant). Compile-only negative
void * from dlsym converted to a function pointer: defined by POSIX, not by ISO C; gcc -pedantic-errors rejects it (the producer's negative.function control)
unsynchronized shared write: ++payload outside the mutex is a data race (TSan reports exactly one race on payload). Do not repair; the repaired variant is the learner's task
hidden-effect callbacks: with P1_EFFECT=1 the comparison callback allocates, with P1_EFFECT=2 the logger waits in poll(); both violate the claimed no-allocation/no-wait contract
deliberate invalid mapped-memory access: SIGSEGV on a PROT_NONE page and SIGBUS past EOF, observed externally; never sanitizer-instrumented; its atoi descriptor selector is part of the specimen
